newsitem.title: USA: American List to merge with Snyder.
newsitem.headline: American List to merge with Snyder.

text.p: American List Corp said Wednesday it had signed a definitive agreement to be acquired by Snyder Communications Inc in a stock swap.

Under the agreement, Snyder will exchange one share for each of American List's 4.5 million shares outstanding if the average trading price of Snyder before the deal closes is at least $32, American List said.
The exchange ratio increases if the trading price is less than $32, Snyder said.
The deal is valued at about $125 million, according to a statement by Snyder, a marketing services company based in Bethesda, Md.
American List, based here, maintains and markets databases of U.S. school students.
The transaction is subject to shareholder and regulatory approval and other customary closing conditions, American List said.
The deal is expected to be completed by the second quarter, it said.

American List said it expects to continue to pay its regularly scheduled dividends until the merger becomes effective. It said its previously announced program to repurchase its common stock is being discontinued.
Martin Lerner, president of American List, said the merger will open "many synergistic opportunities,"
"Snyder's approach to providing integrated marketing solutions offers the ideal platform for expanding the size and scope of both our businesses," he said.
American List also announced that it expects its earnings for the fourth quarter and year ended February 28 to be down from the previous fiscal year.

For the quarter ended February 28, 1996, the company reported revenues of $5.7 million and net income of $0.42 per share. For the year it reported revenues of $18.9 million and net income of $1.68 per share.
Snyder Communications further said it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Brann Holdings Ltd, a direct marketing company in the United Kingdom, in a deal valued at $77.5 million.
Under the agreement, Snyder will issue approximately 2.7 million shares of common stock in exchange for all the outstanding stock of Brann.
The deal includes the assumption of about $5.0 million in debt and will be accounted for as a pooling of interests, Snyder said.

Snyder said the two acquisition will be accretive from the outset. It said it currently expects the acquisitions to be accretive by approximately 20 percent or $0.08 per share and 25 percent or $0.14 per share on a fully diluted basis, over existing consensus analyst estimates for 1997 and 1998, respectively.

The acquisition of Brann Holdings will enhance Snyder's ability to meet the explosive growth in demand for outsourced marketing services on a more globalized basis, said Daniel M. Snyder, chairman and chief executive officer of Snyder Communications.
Brann Holdings, which is privately held, is based in Cirencester. In 1996, it had revenues of approximately $60 million.

Christopher Gater, chief executive officer of Brann, said, "We are extremely pleased to be joining forces with a market leader like Snyder. The combination will leverage both companies' marketing strengths and should result in significant operational synergies."
